title: Which other shapes have four angles of symmetry?
description: The paper windmill looks the same after four different turns about its centre. A square, a plus sign with four equal arms and a pinwheel with four equal blades all match themselves after each quarter turn. Keeko's doubt is that only the windmill has four angles of symmetry, because it is the only thing that spins.
teaching_notes: One idea: a shape has exactly four angles of symmetry when it matches itself after each quarter turn about its centre. Watch for students who link angles of symmetry to things that spin.

source: The windmill has exactly 4 angles of symmetry: 90�, 180�, 27
video_script.why: The child finds other shapes that match themselves after each quarter turn, and sees that having four angles of symmetry depends on the shape, not on whether it spins.
video_script.substitution: Turn each shape by a quarter turn about its centre and check that it lands on itself.
video_script.anchor: a paper windmill with four equal blades and a red point at its centre
video_script.wrong_answer: only the windmill has four angles of symmetry
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says only the windmill has four angles of symmetry, because it is the only thing that spins. A square does not spin by itself, but turned by hand about its centre it lands on itself after each quarter turn.
video_script.payoff_line: A square also has exactly four angles of symmetry

final_answer.value: Yes, a square; also a plus sign made of four equal arms, or a pinwheel with four equal blades
final_answer.spoken: a square also has exactly four angles of symmetry

maths_rules: A turn about the centre after which a shape looks exactly the same is called an angle of symmetry
The full turn of 360 degrees counts as one of the angles of symmetry
A shape with exactly 4 angles of symmetry matches itself after each quarter turn: 90, 180, 270 and 360 degrees
A square, a plus sign with 4 equal arms and a pinwheel with 4 equal blades all match themselves after each quarter turn
video_script.design: One idea: matching itself after each quarter turn gives four angles of symmetry. The windmill stays on the board all video. Wrong idea: only things that spin have angles of symmetry.

narration: <bookmark mark='term'/>Turn a shape about its centre. If it looks exactly the same afterwards, that turn is called an angle of symmetry.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks only the windmill has four angles of symmetry, because it is the only thing that spins.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But a square does not need to spin by itself. Turn it by hand about its centre, and it lands on itself after each quarter turn.
<bookmark mark='shape'/>Angles of symmetry depend on the shape, not on spinning.
